title: Optional Heca public API client and collaboration UI
summary: Bind the same planner project to authorized Heca instances/rooms. Consume live snapshots/chat/actions without owning orchestration.
description:
Purpose: Phase 4 of F025, after P116/P128/P130. Bind the same planner project to Heca rooms over the Heca-initiated restricted duplex: Heca reads planner snapshots/events; Agent Plan shows project -> rooms -> room chat and sends messages through one Heca action, send_message, via Heca's single command door. Only enrolled room agents bind to Heca; Heca owns rooms, chat archive and orchestration. Further reverse actions only per explicit use case; multi-computer use is out of scope.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

- P131(F025)/T497: The Heca connection contract and verified shared-planner bindings.
- P131(F025)/T498: Scoped Heca collaboration snapshots and recoverable live events in Agent Plan.
- P131(F025)/T499: Room chat from Agent Plan through one Heca action, with honest receipts.
- P131(F025)/T500: Collaboration views: project -> rooms -> room chat, member handles with live labels and @ autocomplete.

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

tasks.title: Define the optional execution-runtime contract and shared-planner bindings
tasks.description:
Outcome: The Heca connection contract and verified shared-planner bindings.

Implementation contract:
- Heca initiates the authenticated WebSocket to Agent Plan; consume requests/events on that channel without dialing a Heca listener.
- Restricted duplex: every request from Agent Plan to Heca is an invocation of a Heca action-catalog entry through Heca's single command door, authorised for a dedicated agent-plan principal role. v1: planner reads/events for Heca, room snapshots/events and chat history for Agent Plan, plus one reverse action, send_message. More actions only per explicit use case.
- Only explicitly enrolled room agents gain a verified binding. A manually launched agent in a Heca terminal remains standalone even with generic status reporting. Use session-registration.md for full fields, multiple memberships, late native IDs and Heca server/boot/instance/workspace/member identities.
- Planner permissions never depend on Heca bindings; a dropped channel only marks rooms, members and chat stale/unavailable.
- Support both startup orders with retries in code; no model-driven polling. Multi-computer use (remote endpoint, TLS, pairing) is out of scope.
- Depends on T489/T490 only; execution history (T491) is attached later. Co-owned with Heca-Pro T043 (cross-project dependency not expressible in the planner).

Acceptance: demonstrate the actual integration against Heca-Pro on one computer, in both startup orders; preserve completed historical evidence.

tasks.title: Connect Heca collaboration snapshots and live events to the shared planner view
tasks.description:
Outcome: Scoped Heca collaboration snapshots and recoverable live events in Agent Plan.

Current implementation: Planner entity events cannot describe rooms, worker crashes or chat messages. YAML is desired setup, not live state.

Implementation responsibility:
- Provide project -> linked Heca rooms: read authorized snapshots from Heca-owned state, including instances/rooms/members (stable handle plus live label data)/roles/assignments and optional execution links.
- Use consistent snapshot/cursor bootstrap over the one Heca-initiated connection with project-filtered subscriptions. Persist attributable binding/session changes while Heca stays authoritative for room/chat facts.
- Handle epoch changes, expired cursors, lost events, revocation and slow consumers with explicit gaps/resnapshot and bounded history.
- Forward projections over Agent Plan's own WebSocket; do not turn runtime events into mirrored planner writes or derived done transitions. Neither disconnect nor replay changes execution locks, starts work or creates a second chat database.
- On disconnect show rooms and chat as unavailable and keep last-known data marked stale; task work, native turn, connection and target availability remain distinct.
- No dependency on T493: target availability is attached later.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A new/crashed worker is reflected without reading mutable runtime data from Git/YAML.
- Two projects cannot leak rooms/messages across authorization boundaries.
- Agent Plan continues receiving standalone planner changes while Heca is stopped.

tasks.title: Add attributed room chat and authorized runtime actions for UI and agent clients
tasks.description:
Outcome: Room chat from Agent Plan through one Heca action, with honest receipts.

Current implementation: Agent Plan has no reverse interface to Heca; queuing a native message does not prove delivery or turn/task start.

Implementation responsibility:
- v1 scope: send_message(room, to?, text) only, invoked as a Heca action through the one door under the agent-plan principal role. Plain text; no attachments, no native actions. Read room history pages from Heca's archive.
- Addressing: messages are visible to the whole room but delivered as model input only to addressees: the configured orchestrator by default, @member, or @all for an explicit broadcast. A room without an orchestrator rejects a recipient-less message with a typed no_default_recipient error; the UI asks for @member or @all. Messages queued for a removed orchestrator stay visible as undelivered and are never redirected.
- Agent Plan is not a mesh/room agent and never calls agent-comms or model APIs directly. Heca owns the SQLite chat archive and attachments until explicit deletion. Native transcript aggregation is excluded.
- Use authenticated principal, explicit project/room/destination and request identity; keep long-lived Heca secrets out of browser bundles. Ordinary messages queue without interrupting busy agents.
- Receipts: queued / sent / uncertain, only with evidence; status lookup/idempotency handle acknowledgement loss; no unsafe retries.
- Do not convert chat automatically into Accepted Decisions.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Human and agent authorship remain distinct; an agent cannot impersonate the UI supervisor.
- A non-addressed member receives no model input; @all reaches every member.
- A delivered message never certifies a model turn, task start, test or merge.

tasks.title: Add collaboration views, chat and planner-to-room navigation
tasks.description:
Outcome: Collaboration views in Agent Plan: project -> rooms -> room chat.

Current implementation: Existing sketches show rooms/agents and work/availability; the reviewed prototypes have no room, member or chat screens, so design intake comes first.

Implementation responsibility:
- Navigation: project -> its Heca-linked rooms -> room group chat, with addressing as in T499 (default orchestrator, @member, @all; no-orchestrator rule).
- Agent identity: stable handle (worker-1, orchestrator) for @mentions and history, plus a live label computed at display time (model + current F/P/T, or the free-text title). Typing '@' autocompletes matching members showing model and F/P/T.
- Show room-wide visibility, queued/sent/uncertain and undelivered states, stale runtime and the unavailable state when Heca is disconnected; preserve drafts and destination on navigation.
- Present standalone and room-integrated agent/session/execution attribution and the execution-lock state with the human Release action.
- Reuse Heca message IDs/history through its API; no planner chat archive. Keep resume/planner/graph/code views usable without Heca. Heca native/WebView hosting is external owner work.
- Code/editor links (T487/T488) are an optional later extension, not a dependency.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Collaboration controls appear only for available authorized capabilities and show explicit unavailability.
- '@wo' suggests the matching workers with model and F/P/T.
- The same real Heca messages are visible in both products, with no shadow room/orchestrator store.
